source.title: Regime-wise analysis of generalization dynamics in mutual learning through double descent
source.authors: Fumika Komori; Keiichi Nakanishi; Terumasa Tokunaga

page_placements.theme: Structural and training interventions shift or suppress peaks

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present and readable. The text contains inconsistent DOI strings and placeholder dates, but these do not prevent extracting the results.
record.tranche_reason: It varies CNN model width and measures test error against model size, and also measures test-error dynamics over epochs, using the double-descent curve method in new training settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports model-width sweeps and epoch-wise test-error behavior. It also measures noisy-label and clean-label training errors and prediction variance. Hessian and loss-landscape results are not included because they do not directly measure a claim version. The plotted results do not give extractable numeric values.
record.test_reason: It sweeps the width of a 5-layer CNN (k=1–40) under 20% label noise and measures final-epoch test error. This is the original Nakkiran et al. model-wise setup. It also reports epoch-wise test-error dynamics per regime, on four image datasets, for individual learning and mutual learning.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that ML's effect is regime-dependent and strongest in the CPR near the interpolation threshold. There ML suppresses noisy-label fitting, reaches flatter minima, lowers prediction variance and lowers test error. In the OPR the final error difference is small but local geometry differs.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a 5-layer CNN width sweep and test-error measurement, but compares mutual learning with individual learning across four image datasets, adds 20% training-label noise, and analyzes regime-specific dynamics.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported ML-versus-IL differences depend on parameter-wise regime: small in UPR, most pronounced in CPR, and generally small in final test error in OPR. Hessian behavior in OPR also varies by dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Mutual learning slows fitting of noisy-label training samples more than clean-label samples, mainly in the critically-parameterized regime.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mutual learning delays memorization of mislabeled examples near the interpolation threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Mutual learning suppresses the model-wise test-error peak and shifts the interpolation threshold and regime boundaries to larger widths on all four datasets (e.g., CIFAR-10 OPR starts at k=12 for IL vs k=14 for ML).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A co-training consistency loss shifts the double-descent peak to larger model sizes and lowers its height.

fits_no_version.finding: In the CPR, ML reaches flatter minima than IL, with smaller top Hessian eigenvalues and flatter loss landscapes. In the OPR the pattern is dataset-dependent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Solutions near the interpolation threshold are sharper, and peak-suppressing training finds flatter minima there.

record.peer_reviewed: Nonlinear Theory and Its Applications IEICE
record.problems: The plotted curves do not provide extractable numeric error values. Results are averaged over five runs, the regime boundaries are operationally defined, and the experiments use one CNN architecture and a fixed 20% label-noise setting. The variance results are observational comparisons, not a causal test.

untested.parts: Only one architecture family (5-layer CNN width); other deep architectures and parameter-count axes are not tested.
Epoch-wise shape is stated explicitly only for CIFAR-10 at k=40; it is not stated for the other datasets.
No non-deep model classes are tested.
No effective-complexity measure is computed or used to predict peak location.
Noise level is fixed at 20% and not varied. Multiple peaks are not examined. No tuned regularization sweep is run. Mutual learning suppresses the peak but is not an optimally tuned regularizer.
There is no recount of effective parameters.

missing.what: Numeric regime boundaries locating the interpolation threshold: CIFAR-10 IL CPR k=5–11 and OPR from k=12; ML CPR k=6–13 and OPR from k=14. Other datasets are in Table A-I (e.g., CIFAR-100 IL OPR from k=19, ML from k=21).
missing.locator: Section 3.3, Fig. 3; Appendix A, Table A-I

record.verdict_notes: Double descent is a tool here for studying mutual learning, but the IL baseline replicates the Nakkiran et al. width-sweep setup, which justifies T1 for V1 and V2. All results are figure-only, averaged over five runs, with no extractable numbers. The V2 limits_scope verdict reflects the model-size dependence that Nakkiran et al. also reported. The V6 support is weak and correlational. The ML–IL variance rows in the UPR and OPR were unlinked.

versions.untested_parts: The study varies CNN width, not parameter counts across different deep-network architectures; interpolation is operationally defined using training error below 0.01.
Epoch-wise behavior is analyzed within parameter-wise regimes; the reported epoch-wise double descent is specifically in the over-parameterized regime.
Training sample count is not varied.
Only a 5-layer CNN architecture is studied; the claim across model classes is not tested.
The study does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
The study uses 20% label noise and measures prediction variance, but does not vary noise levels, test multiple peaks, or tune regularization to test whether peaks disappear.
The study does not recalculate complexity using an effective number of parameters.
